results.claim: One round has the exact form T(p)=reverse(p_i : i in D) followed by (p_i : i not in D), where D={i>=2 : p_i<p_{i-1}} and both subsequences otherwise retain index order.
results.proof_sketch: The marked elements are precisely the descent bottoms indexed by D. They are moved to the front in increasing index order. Each new move precedes all earlier moves, so their final order is decreasing index order. Removing and moving them does not change the relative order of unmarked elements.

results.claim: There is an exact reduction of every maximum-element phase to parallel deletion in a word. Once i+1,...,n are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. Define A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j : 2<=j<=s and r_{j-1}<r_j). The number of further rounds until i is fixed is h(R)=min{t:A^t(R) is empty}.
results.proof_sketch: Element i is never marked. The first element of R is marked because it is smaller than i; a later r_j is marked exactly when r_j<r_{j-1}. Thus the elements remaining to the right of i after the round are exactly A(R), independently of L. Iteration proves the formula. Moreover h is computable in one scan: start a stack with sentinel +infinity. For each x, pop while the top value is smaller than x, let tau(x)=1 plus the largest tau among popped entries (zero if none), and push (x,tau(x)). The stack remains decreasing in value, and induction on the scan shows tau(x) is exactly x's deletion round. Hence h=max tau.

results.claim: If W(n) is the worst-case number of nontrivial rounds, then W(n)<=n(n-1)/2. Consequently no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds.
results.proof_sketch: Decompose an execution into phases for active maxima n,n-1,...,2, assigning zero length when a maximum is already fixed. In the phase for i, the word R in the preceding claim has at most i-1 elements. Parallel deletion removes at least one element per nonempty round, so h(R)<=|R|<=i-1. Therefore W(n)<=sum_{i=2}^n(i-1)=n(n-1)/2. In particular W(n)/n^2<=1/2-1/(2n), which rules out little-omega(n^2). This sharpens the stated quadratic round bound by its lower-order term.

results.claim: For p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1) and n>=3, at least n-1+floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) rounds are required.
results.proof_sketch: Let B_0 be empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m). Induction with the round formula gives T^t(p_n)=B_t, n, t+1,...,n-1 for 0<=t<=n-1. Hence n first fixes after n-1 rounds, leaving B_{n-1},n. Apply the deletion-stack characterization to B_m. A simultaneous induction on m shows that its largest deletion label is the unique q satisfying q(q+1)/2<=m<(q+1)(q+2)/2. One explicit stronger invariant is: writing m=q(q+1)/2+r, the final decreasing stack has consecutive values, and its deletion labels are (1,q,q-1,...,q-r,q-r-2,...,1) for r<=q-2, and (1,q,q-1,...,1) for r=q-1 or q. Thus the next active maximum needs q further rounds. Substituting m=n-1 proves the bound.

results.claim: Under the zero-no-op-round convention, the exact worst-case values for n=1,...,9 are 0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.
results.proof_sketch: Exhaustive enumeration evaluated every permutation using the exact round map in Claim 1. For n=2,...,8, (n,1,...,n-1) attains the listed maximum. For n=9, (3,9,4,5,1,2,6,7,8) attains 26 rounds. Exhaustion supplies the matching upper bounds.

final_writeup:
Let W(n) denote the maximum number of genuine transformations before reaching the identity permutation. The literal superquadratic subquestion has a definitive negative answer: W(n)<=n(n-1)/2, so W(n) is never omega(n^2).

The useful structural reduction is to examine the current largest unfixed value i. If the active prefix is L i R, its right suffix evolves autonomously by repeatedly retaining only ascent tops: A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j:r_{j-1}<r_j). Therefore the duration of that phase is exactly the extinction time of R under A. A monotone-stack algorithm assigns every entry its exact extinction round in linear time. Consequently the entire round count is the sum of these stack heights over successive active maxima.

This yields the quadratic universal bound immediately and also gives exact analysis of initial phases of concrete families. In particular, (n,1,...,n-1) needs n-1 rounds merely to fix n, followed by at least floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) rounds to fix n-1. Exact enumeration gives W(1),...,W(9)=0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.

These results do not determine the asymptotically tight order: the proved lower bound here remains linear, while the universal upper bound is quadratic. Thus the full target remains open, but any interpretation asking for a genuinely superquadratic number of rounds is incompatible with the phase bound.
